<details><summary>Help — recovery and positive margins</summary>

A positive greater-than margin means that the total probability of valid
later suffixes exceeds that of earlier/equal suffixes. It does **not** mean
the most likely token is a valid year. Keep whole-vocabulary normalization,
raw probability difference and numeric probability mass visible.

</details>

<!-- ARENA:cell code -->

```python
import hashlib

GT_SELECTION_RULE = {"minimum_recovery": .85, "maximum_positive_margin_drop": .10, "maximum_kl": .5}

if RUN_REAL_EDGES:
    gt_full_development = gt_development_behavior(gt_dev_engine.clean_logits)

    def gt_qualifies(row):
        return (row["recovery"] >= GT_SELECTION_RULE["minimum_recovery"]
                and row["fraction_positive_probability_difference"] >= (
                    gt_full_development["fraction_positive_probability_difference"]
                    - GT_SELECTION_RULE["maximum_positive_margin_drop"])
                and row["kl_clean_to_circuit"] <= GT_SELECTION_RULE["maximum_kl"])

    if not gt_qualifies(gt_acdc_development):
        raise RuntimeError("The greater-than ACDC development candidate failed; keep the result and do not open transfer.")
    gt_selected_masks = {"acdc": gt_acdc_mask.clone()}
    gt_selected_development = {"acdc": gt_acdc_development}
    for method in gt_scores:
        eligible_rows = [row for row in gt_curve_rows if gt_qualifies(row["methods"][method])]
        if not eligible_rows:
            raise RuntimeError(f"No development budget qualifies for {method}; do not select from transfer.")
        chosen = min(eligible_rows, key=lambda row: row["edge_count"])
        gt_selected_masks[method] = top_edge_mask(gt_dev_engine.graph, gt_scores[method], chosen["edge_count"])
        gt_selected_development[method] = chosen["methods"][method]

    gt_frozen_choices = {
        "model_revision": GPT2_REVISION, "criteria": GT_SELECTION_RULE,
        "discovery_prompts": gt_discovery["prompts"], "development_prompts": gt_development["prompts"],
        "transfer_seed": 13, "transfer_count": 64, "transfer_split": "heldout",
        "choices": {method: {"active_edges": mask.nonzero().tolist(),
                             "development": gt_selected_development[method]}
                    for method, mask in gt_selected_masks.items()},
    }
    frozen_text = json.dumps(gt_frozen_choices, sort_keys=True, indent=2) + "\n"
    gt_freeze_hash = hashlib.sha256(frozen_text.encode()).hexdigest()
    gt_freeze_path = edge_run_directory / "frozen-greater-than" / f"{gt_freeze_hash}.json"
    gt_freeze_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if gt_freeze_path.exists() and gt_freeze_path.read_text() != frozen_text:
        raise RuntimeError("A frozen selection record must not be overwritten.")
    gt_freeze_path.write_text(frozen_text)
    display(pd.DataFrame([{"method": method, "edges": int(mask.sum()),
                           **{key: gt_selected_development[method][key] for key in
                              ("recovery", "fraction_positive_probability_difference", "kl_clean_to_circuit")}}
                          for method, mask in gt_selected_masks.items()]))
    print(f"Choices frozen before transfer: {gt_freeze_path}")
```

### Limitations and connection to the papers

These are small, controlled GPT-2 studies with 32 discovery examples. The
greater-than holdout changes one wording pattern; it does not test broad
distribution shift. The reference IOI study has no held-out result because
none of its four candidates met the development criteria. Its diagnostic
plots reuse development examples and must not be described as transfer.
The graph contains additive residual connections and fixed component internals;
it does not discover neuron-level structure or attention links between token
positions. Corrupt substitutions can create activations unlike ordinary text,
and results depend on the corruption, metric, greedy order and finite IG grid.

ACDC gives local deletion decisions, not a globally minimal graph. EAP and
EAP-IG rank local or path-averaged first-order effects; nonlinear interactions
can make those rankings poor circuit selectors. Exact edge counts here include
all selected legal edges. The output-frontier selector does not subsequently
prune nodes without an input path, so its budgets must not be equated with a
paper's post-pruning budgets. The sampled completeness probes are bounded
counterfactual tests, not proof over every possible circuit subset.

The full graph uses 32,491 **additive** edges. Fixed connections inside a
component are rerun rather than counted as removable edges. Do not compare this
count directly with a graph convention that also counts fixed direct edges.
The [ACDC paper](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/file/34e1dbe95d34d7ebaf99b9bcaeb5b2be-Paper-Conference.pdf)
and [authors' code](https://github.com/ArthurConmy/Automatic-Circuit-Discovery)
provide the wider experimental context. The numerical parity check uses the
[EAP-IG implementation at a fixed commit](https://github.com/hannamw/EAP-IG/tree/e24bafd3d22af2c59ac5a83e0a6581b89b5c05dd),
including its left-endpoint input-interpolation grid. Matching those scores
validates the implementation under matched inputs; it does not imply that a
small circuit faithfully recovers every task.
